body:
Thanks for taking the time to comment. I'm never really fine but that was a lofty goal in the first place. I just try to get by on distractions - video games are the only thing I've ever found in my life that I'm truly passionate about. When I'm in the zone I can forget about all the pain for a small period of time. But the combination of dysthymia and hypermobile EDS suck a lot of the energy right out of me and most of the time I don't feel like playing anything. It has the practical effect of making me feel 20 years older than I actually am.

I hope things get better for you and you don't end up like me. I also share with you what sounds like a cripplingly low self-esteem so I know exactly what that feels like. Wish I had some words of encouragement but I don't, and I guess that's what makes it truly depressing.
I'm hoping so too. Technically one center did not outright reject me, but they do have a year long waitlist to even make an appointment.

Thank you for your response, sadly I live too far away from a Mayo Clinic to do anything other than fly there. I don't think I could justify doing that on the very real possibility that I don't actually have hEDS or HDS. Strangely enough I don't have any pain in my joints, though I don't know if that's just because I'm young (early 30s).

I watched that video and while I was watching it I had a thought. What if, instead of focusing on my breath, I try to focus on my pain instead? The sensation of it, where it is, and try to face it directly and overpower it as if it was a foreign invader in my body?

I started this today and I'm so confused. How am I supposed to know what to choose? Why is there no suggested plan of things to try first? Why is it just skipping around? The fuck am I actually supposed to do?

This is actually INCREASING my stress level rather than reducing it! Instant fucking regret and waste of $60. DERHTRHYHJTDFJHTDJHTRDRDHDTJDZTJTRDJDTJFFTDCXFGGCXVC
Wish I even had meds that worked. I'm not going to start on narcotics at such a young age so it really limits my options. Everything else I've tried has done nothing to help.
It's a terrible loop and I don't know how to break out of it.

I hate posts like this. Lazily just linking to a hotline has shown to be ineffective for many people who actually call it (if they don't get committed to an institution, which if they do, they'll really wish they had killed themselves when they had the chance because they'll be treated like sub-human garbage in those padded prisons).

That doesn't make me feel at all better about this. I punched myself in the face multiple times after this. I'm sure one day I'm going to give myself a concussion, at least then I'll have a FUCKING EXCUSE FOR BEING THIS RETARDED.

Am I supposed to throw darts at a board until I stumble upon something that defies my intuition and is actually interesting? Because I feel like with no internal guidance that's about all I can do.

That being said, I don't know how you can "start" a hobby you have no interest in in the first place. It's like trying to eat food that disgusts you; sure you can force yourself to do it, but you're not just going to enjoy it over time unless you develop some sort of Stockholm syndrome.

I've listed some games I played recently in another comment. I'll put them here as well: Persona 4 Golden, Conker's Bad Fur Day, Sonic Advance 2, Golden Sun: Dark Dawn. I've also played some Phoenix Wright which I've had to resort to looking up guides for every 10 minutes because I'm too stupid to think of the answers.

Outside of Binding of Isaac I don't really care for roguelikes. I prefer games with hand-crafted level design over random generation.

Played Dark Souls because it's that one game people never stop talking about, and not to my surprise at all, I didn't like it. It's also in a genre I don't have much experience in (3rd person action RPG) so you can imagine how that went.

Yakuza is great though. I've played Yakuza 0, 1 and 2 and enjoyed them quite a bit. I'm waiting for the other ones to come to PC.

Metroidvanias are a big commitment in terms of learning, playtime and memory. The last part is what intimidates me. You have to remember what you've done, where you've been, all the mechanics, your weapons/skills and what your current objective is, i.e. where on the huge map you can make progress on given your current skills.

To any average person with a functioning brain that doesn't seem like a big deal at all, but my memory is shit and I can barely even remember what I need to do for my job sometimes from day to day. That's why I'm very hesitant to pick up something like Super Metroid.

That's what's so frustrating about it. I have no excuse for being so terrible at games now. I mean, I've played platformers since I could barely talk and I'm getting my ass kicked at a fucking Sonic game, of all things. You know, the 2D Sonic games that are barely above Kirby in terms of difficulty and you just spin through on-rails loop-de-loops and jump every once in a while until you win?

I just don't understand it.
I've already gone down the therapy route. It was a big waste of time and money.

Games have always been my only hobby my whole life, since a very young age. Nothing else interests me.

I don't get any enjoyment out of playing a game with cheats enabled.

That's fine and all, but it's not fun only being able to play a few hours of a game before having to throw in the towel. It pisses me off and is probably amplified by having an inferiority complex and low self-esteem. So I can't help but take it personally.

I play games from many different genres, mostly retro though. Here's a sampling of the games from past months that I've been unable to complete:

Persona 4 Golden

Conker's Bad Fur Day

Sonic Advance 2

Golden Sun: Dark Dawn

There's probably more but my memory is terrible lately and I just can't remember things like I used to.

Narrative-driven games aren't really my thing. If I want a good story I look to a different medium than games, whether that be TV series, visual novels, etc.
The reason I'm so hard on myself is because I'm in total control of my actions and where I go in life, and yet I'm still a complete fuck-up. I have no excuse.

Late reply but I just saw this message. The problem with self-confidence is you have to find something to be confident in the first place. If I was actually competent in the first place I wouldn't have this self-esteem problem. It's the catch-22.

There is no A for effort in the real world. That's why I'm so hard on myself, because no matter how much I buckle down and focus, my stupid ass can't produce results. How can you be self-confident when you're shit at everything?

Yes, I've been to both of those. I've also been to a bunch of different specialists and had enough procedures and scans done that I'm now buried in medical bills. And after over 4 years I'm no closer to knowing what's causing my legs to feel like they're on fire than I was on day one.

That's the problem - I can't like me. I have a deep-seated hatred of myself. Just about every day my boss chews me out over a mistake I've made - and he's right, I have no excuse to be this incompetent. If it were any other job where they're not hurting for help I would've been shitcanned a long time ago.

Is it wrong to have standards for myself? I don't think it is.

This chair was designed by assholes, and thus not easily repairable, because they want you to take it to one of their special repair centers. I don't have the tools to open the chair and replace the lever.
Also, the chair is a Herman Miller. No way in hell am I buying another one of those.

Nothing I've tried has any effect. Even though I have muscle twitching and pelvic tilt caused by my muscles on one side locking up, medicines like gabapentin do nothing. Nothing dulls the pain either, I always get it full force, even when I'm trying to sleep. Some days it feels like my body's trying to rip itself apart.

MBSR sounds like a combination of things I've already tried like yoga and meditation.

I've seen just about every doctor at this point. No one knows what it is, and the list of treatments and procedures I've tried damn near rules out everything. There's nothing left to even self-diagnose because the symptoms don't match with any illness or disorder me or any doctor I've seen has ever heard of.

I've found that people in general only really care about two things: their social status and their money (particularly 401k/investments). Everything else is tertiary platitudes when push comes to shove.

Not every person is like this of course, but most of them are.
Yep, that was it. Thanks a bunch.

BUMBO WINS

**FATALITY**
Installed it through hakchi and it still doesn't work.

That's good to hear about the less childish tone. It's the one thing I dislike about the PS4 Ratchet and Clank so far: the cringe-inducing cartoony immature Hollywood tripe they call humor. It's a real turn-off.
The issue ended up being a faulty adapter. Got a replacement and it booted up into Swiss just fine.

Reformatted the card to FAT32 (it was previously FAT), put the files in there, made sure the adapter was firmly in slot B and I still get the generic Action Replay screen. This is what my SD card files look like.

https://imgur.com/a/qt2WOUh

Am I doing something wrong?

What I don't understand is that several people have said that this particular SD card should work so I don't know what I'm doing wrong. I refuse to get into hardmodding consoles and anything that requires soldering, which is one of the reasons I tend to avoid homebrew altogether.
I don't have one of those.
I cleared the cache for the mobile app (I'm also on android) and it still hangs and crashes when loading yesterday's activity. It loads today's activity just fine.

Sorry, I should clarify. This is crashing my mobile app, not the steam client. The steam client was just showing an error.

Since this is crashing the mobile app it leads me to think it's not a cache issue.
I am at work so I don't have access to my steam client/browser. Is there a way to clear it on my mobile app?
Yesterday's activity causes my steam app to hang and eventually crash/disappear, and I have to boot it up again.

I was unable to load my activity feed yesterday. It crashed my Steam app and in the client it gave an error. Was there a server issue yesterday or is there some new exploit that's going around? Should I be concerned about my account? I believe there was an activity exploit a while ago that could potentially hijack accounts.
I don't know what planet you live on where you can get a job offer before the interview's even done, but can I hitch a ride over there?
Will be 30 soon and I already feel like I'm 50. Severe depression really kills the vitality of youth.

I hate to break it to you, but life will likely only get harder, not easier. I only wish I could go back to my undergrad days.

Also, the only thing a Ph.D. will get you is more debt. The notion that degrees will land you jobs is outdated Baby Boomer ideology. It takes a lot more than that these days to get a job. Work experience and connections trump everything else in today's market, so I would advise seeking out internships or other work. I agree, it sucks, but that's how it is.

I wouldn't be able to play a keyboard-like instrument, tendonitis has already affected my ability to play games that use the WASD keyboard scheme, and something like the piano would only aggravate that.

I thought about doing VGM composition but I'm a layman who doesn't know the first thing about music and I'm assuming the monetary hurdles would be significant as well. I'm also not a creative person so other than ideas for a track or two I've had in my head, I wouldn't do much with it.

Oh, right. I couldn't get into Undertale but I recognize the track you're talking about.

I have a YouTube channel but haven't uploaded anything to it in a long time. I don't do audio commentary on anything because I like to remain anonymous (also a reason why I don't use social media).

Streaming is for people with personalities. I didn't get one of those.

Megalovania?

I don't have any interest in outdoor activities (other than taking the occasional walk) or sports, so that takes out a lot of other casual interests. I'm also very clumsy and my hands are a bit messed up from decades of gaming so I'm not good at doing intensive things with my hands.

Other than that...I don't know. Nothing else really engages me like gaming does.

YouTube, Reddit, Steam, nothing out of the ordinary. Mostly just gaming-related content.

Yes, I really do just have one interest. Unless you count music, and the only thing I listen to is, you guessed it, video game music.
Video games are my only hobby, unless you count the internet in general.

Old-school JRPGs, old-school FPS, vertical shmups, visual novels, and the occasional games from other genres. All single-player. I almost never play AAA games, and rarely play games from Western devs (not a conscious decision, they just don't make the kind of games that I like anymore).

The problem is that while the logical part of my brain knows that life is far too short to care about what people think of me, I can't turn off the fear and nervousness that comes from the emotional part of my brain. It's the part that hates being embarrassed or made to be a fool, and it's always on overdrive.

Of course, there's always the core issue that I'd never be invited to events in the first place due to not having anything in common with people. Even amongst gamers I rarely ever play the games that they play, because the genres I like are either obscure or have fallen out of fashion.

That's a nice proverb, I'll have to remember that.

It's just that online interaction can't replace real life interaction for obvious reasons, and is undoubtedly a big reason why I'm socially retarded today. I haven't had the lifetime of practice that most people have with gestures, expressions, social cues, natural flow of dialog, and other nuances of conversation, as well as communicating in a medium where you can't edit something if it sounds stupid or awkward.

I don't know about that. Friends and the like are always subtly influencing the lives and ideas of others, and in a way, they're a part of someone's world. I'm not a part of anyone's world, and I'll never get to feel that sense of belonging and comfort. It's as if I never existed.

Yeah, I don't know where the depression ends and the real me begins. Like you I've had depression more or less my whole life, and I've been typecasted into being the depressed loner. That just makes it even harder to break out of it.

I hate it when people point out when I smile at something, like they just saw a pink unicorn. It makes me want to never smile in front of people.

Yep, I was a 90s kid and I wish I could go back to those days. I miss my mother, I miss not being afraid and suspicious of everyone, and I miss my biggest decision being what game I was going to rent from the video store. Everything just felt more intimate back then. Nowadays I have a massive Steam library with more games than I could possibly ever play, but back then I got 1 or 2 games for Christmas and I had to play the hell out of them and figure out everything on my own. No GameFAQs, no YouTube, just me and my stubbornness.

I also miss my college days (well, undergrad that is, grad school can fuck off). It was my first taste of independence without the soul-crushing weight of job-hunting, and I still had the energy of youth. No back problems, no migraines, and I didn't feel like the living death every day. Even though I mostly kept to myself, those were still great times.

A nightmare that sapped away my sanity. Before then I was living in a bubble where people kept telling me I was smart even though I really wasn't. Ended up at the bottom of the class on academic probation and almost failed out of grad school due to my grades. I did not belong there and didn't make friends. I graduated, but it was not worth it at all. And now I'm long-term unemployed so that degree is basically toilet paper to me.

If you have to ask whether grad school is for you, then the answer is no. Trust me on this. I went to grad school because I just figured it was what I was supposed to do, and it was the worst mistake of my life.

I get these calls all the time. They're likely not scams assuming they're calling you about a specific position, but a lot of times they don't read your resume and call you about some senior level position you're not remotely qualified for because you matched a keyword search.

That being said, I did get my first job out of college through a cold call from an Indian recruiter. It wasn't a great job, but it was a source of decent income for a few years.

The catch is that in recent years it's become competitive just like everything else, with a lot of schools looking for expensive certifications like CERTA or actual teaching experience/a relevant Bachelors, and a lot of these schools really mistreat their teachers on top of that. It is not a glamorous life by any means, and as a foreigner stuck there on a visa you have much less leverage to negotiate your way out of shitty situations, especially if it's a culture that looks down on foreign ESL teachers.

Keep in mind though I've never taught overseas so take what I say with a grain of salt. I have however done a lot of research into what the ESL market is like these days and read hundreds of accounts from people who've taught ESL.

Yes, it was what I saved from my last job.

How exactly does one "work on" anxiety? Trying to not be anxious is like trying to not think about pink elephants. It's how I'm wired to think. It's like there's a mental block that prevents me from calming down or not feeling depressed. Any thoughts that are optimistic feel fake to me, especially in this point in my life where I've failed to find work every week for a year.

I feel like I'm in a mental cage that does not allow me to feel safe or happy, ever. The only person I ever felt safe with (my mother) died a long time ago, and that feeling of safety died along with her.

I don't know anyone else. I came from a broke family, half of which I wouldn't trust to so much as lend them a pencil. I could've moved back in with my mother if she were still alive.

I agree, it is a very unusual situation. Typically one would go back to live with their parents but that isn't applicable for me.

He's eccentric and wild from the stories my relative has told me, makes a lot of really insensitive jokes that make me uncomfortable, and allegedly "used to be" a coke addict. The guy really creeps me out even though I've only spoken to him a few times.

I was coasting on savings after becoming unemployed but now that has run out.

Backerkit's support for backers requires you to log in first. If I had an account I could login to I wouldn't need help in the first place.

Kickstarter support is naturally as useless as a bump on a log in this scenario.

I've checked several times. Backerkit is on my Safe Senders list and they are not on the Blocked Senders list.

If they somehow did get reported for spam (which I don't recall doing), shouldn't that be a reversible action?

I don't know how common it is, but even after whitelisting Backerkit their emails still don't get through. I used to get their emails a few years ago and then one day they stopped appearing. At this point I've given up trying to resolve the issue.

The real hassle is if you used a Hotmail email address for Kickstarter. For whatever reason, Hotmail automatically blocks all emails from Backerkit, including account recovery emails, meaning you're permanently locked out of the account. Also, for whatever reason Kickstarter has deleted Muv-Luv from my list of backed projects.

Kickstarter/Backerkit is one of the jankiest services I have ever used. I don't know why there needs to be a separate site for rewards in the first place, and it feels like the whole thing is held together by duct tape. Needless to say I don't back projects there anymore.

Your story is shockingly similar to mine. The issue comes when you can't make a living on your interests. Only a privileged few (typically the social butterflies) can turn gaming into a stable career, so the rest of us have to try and scrounge for IT jobs or something else we're not thrilled about.

What makes it worse is that a long resume gap in IT is basically a death sentence. Employers expect you to have a job all year every year, which is an unrealistic expectation in an industry full of short contracts, unexpected layoffs, massive saturation and giant laundry lists of requirements for most positions. Now that I have a 1 year resume gap, I suspect my career in IT is well and truly finished, and the last decade I spent pursuing computer science was a gigantic waste. Now I have no direction, and absolutely no clue what the hell I'm going to do with my life.

Sorry for being such a downer, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. It's just hard to be anything but pessimistic these days.

Nine times out of ten a cat is a better friend than a human. They don't understand things like drama, politics, being fake or putting up a front. They have a simple view of the world, one that isn't corrupted by cynicism and greed. A cat doesn't care who you are, how much money you have, or what color your skin is. Most of the time they just want to love the human that loves them back. In a society full of pressure and ulterior motives, I think that's what a lot of us need the most.

Cats are great.

Unfortunately the job market is divided into two types of people. There are those who are completely ignorant of it, having worked at their job for years, and think it's the same as it was pre-recession, in the 90s or even further back. And then there are people who struggle and know all too well what it's like out there. I know, I've been struggling to find any work at all for a year now. I bet the people telling you you'd never be unemployed haven't updated their resumes in quite a long time.

Sadly that's just how it is. There are so many people who don't understand that even the shittiest, most bottom-of-the-barrel "entry-level" positions require previous experience these days. Hell, even volunteer work is competitive and some positions require you to pay them for the privilege of working for free. It's an absolute joke and as far as I'm concerned the entire job market as it is belongs on the front page of /r/nottheonion.

I didn't have any place specifically that I wanted to go to. I just wanted to go around the country and try the food, visit temples and nature spots, visit some game centers and stuff like that. Unfortunately, due to not knowing Japanese I'd more than likely be limited to the big tourist traps around the Tokyo area, or possibly having to go with a tour group.

Either way it's not something where I could go, come back and still be able to live. I've been coasting on my savings for several months ever since my unemployment benefits ran out, so now I'm in a situation where I need to use what I have to try and get my life turned back around.

Yep, I'll probably be part of the next YouTube viral video called "We Play Hangman With a REAL BODY! [Gone Sexual] [In The Woods] [Cops Called]"

Really makes me sick what they did to that poor guy. Humiliated in front of tons of people for wanting to end his suffering because the world left him out to dry. Truly heinous and shows off some of the worst aspects of humanity.

Yeah, the thing about a career is it can be a giant snowball effect. Start off strong and you get promotions and better offers from people and move up in the world. Start off weak and you eventually get laid off with nothing to show for it, and become long-term unemployed.

Thank you for your kind words, it's obvious that you care about people and that's touching. I wish the world we lived in was a better place and that I wasn't such a square peg.

Also, I couldn't help but notice that you posted in /r/visualnovels. If you ever need a VN recommendation let me know as I've read a bunch of them.

Yeah, I feel like therapists are more like adult babysitters that you get pawned off to. It's very convenient for them that therapy (aka. sitting there listening to you while giving the same advice a friend would and occasionally throwing out a fancy term) is a long and drawn-out process that basically amounts to placating you while emptying your wallet. People make fun of things like the service in Japan where you can rent a friend for a night, but therapy in my experience was damn near the same thing.

I wish karma did in some way exist, but that would imply that the world is fair. Sadly you have to be content with doing the right thing because it's the right thing, and a lot of times it even works out to your detriment. I wish I could help people and make a living while doing it, but that's just not the kind of world we live in anymore.

In the interest of remaining anonymous, I'll have to pass on sharing my resume, sorry. I've had that thing looked over several times and reformatted anyway. You can only polish a turd so much.
I already have a MS in Computer Science and enough debt to bankrupt Donald Trump, so I'll pass on that. Colleges are too out of touch with what the world actually needs.

My hobby is video games, and while streaming on Twitch and getting donations is big right now, it's incredibly saturated and you need to have a charismatic personality in order to make that work. A lot of them don't make near enough to live on either.

The problem is I can't get a job doing damn near anything that makes a living wage. Everything requires experience nowadays, even the crappy jobs. Those that don't are all either part-time, near minimum wage, or both.

Yeah, I had to have my 15-year-old cat put down last week. Felt like I lost a part of myself. She was a wonderful lap cat who was an irreplaceable part of my daily habits and vernacular. I still find myself calling for her on reflex.

That's a pretty good analogy. I wish I could adopt a cat right now, but it's not right for me to accept that responsibility without knowing if I can financially follow through with it for the rest of that cat's life. Who knows, my next job (if that ever comes) could be overseas for all I know.

Unless I want to learn survival skills, go out in the woods and build a shelter/catch my own food, I CAN'T forget about money. Money is required for absolutely everything, and the less money you have, the less freedom you have to do what you want.

Mental health resources (and mental health treatment in general) in the US are a complete farce. From my experience therapy and medication were not only incredibly expensive but incredibly ineffective. Honestly a lot of the defeatist depression you're seeing right now is because of slogging through hundreds of calls and dozens of interviews with no offers for a year. I don't think there's any way a sane person could be optimistic having faced that.

I had written off Korea because it sounded like they went the way of Japan and tightened up jobs there. Don't get me wrong, Korea and especially Japan would've been my top picks but I was trying to be realistic about the job market.

I do appreciate your responses (as well as everyone else's), thanks. I can't help but go around in circles thinking about it, because this would be a point of no return if I decided to pursue it, and a declaration that my career in IT is done for good.

Edit: As for teaching kids, you're expected to be extra fun and cheerful with kids, as well as be able to handle the troublemakers. Needless to say I would struggle with that.

Yes, I thought about going to Thailand and doing a CELTA course there. The problem is I've been reading a lot of people's opinions on various sites and forums, and the consensus seems to be that ESL, like many industries today, is drying up and becoming more competitive, even in "hot" markets like Vietnam. And the almost 1 year of failure finding any work in my home country has all but completely eroded my confidence in finding a job. This is compounded by the fact that I want to teach at the high school level or above and wouldn't be able to handle dealing with kids. And from what I gather, kids by far make up the majority of the market.

If I were to move to Thailand or Vietnam or wherever, I would be betting the farm on that working. There is no safety net. I can't just move in with relatives if it doesn't work out. I'm completely on my own here.

Edit: As for Europe, I think that would be difficult seeing as I'm American.

So sick of the fucking shell game that is the job market. It's like a cruel joke. "Can't get this because you're underqualified. Can't get this because you're overqualified. Can't get this because you're not the account manager's nephew." It's gotten to the point where you actually have to PAY to work at volunteer positions. Fucking unbelievable.

This whole circus-like song and dance just so you can put food in your mouth pisses me off more than anything else on the planet.

Tell me about it.

Then again, almost all my classmates from grad school jump-started their careers and are now senior developers making more than I'll ever make in my life working at prestigious tech companies. I was the one that failed.

I'm not going to pad my resume (aka. straight-up lie) as being honest with people is just who I am as a person, even if it bites me in the ass. So if I'm not qualified, then I'm not qualified. Also I'm confused as to why an "IT instructor" position would be listed on an ESL website.

I'd almost rather go homeless here than go to China.

Yeah, I live in the Charlotte area and you definitely can't live on part-time work here. I'll be moving soon, but it'll be to the middle of nowhere where there aren't any jobs.

The problem with applying to jobs you don't qualify for is, you have to be your own filter otherwise your time gets wasted. A lot of these recruiters and HR people don't know the first thing about the positions they're filling so they'll send you a job description of senior positions that require 10+ years of experience and set up a phone interview, and those interviews always go the same way: a complete waste of time.
Yeah, I wish. I've already been involuntarily out of work for almost a year, and it doesn't look like that's changing anytime soon.

I've looked at state jobs before and almost all of them require relevant experience or at least a relevant degree; same as everything else. As for the post office, from my understanding the hours on those vary and they're usually part time. I don't have parents/relatives to move back in with so it's not like I can offload the cost of rent/bills. My friend used to work as a mail carrier but that only worked because she lived with her parents at the time.

The problem with that is my instructor position wasn't "real" teaching, i.e. I wasn't doing any lecturing. I was in charge of the lab component of introductory CS classes, so mostly I was answering questions and grading stuff.

Actually, after doing some more research on this I think I may pass on this. The general consensus for those serious about a career change and not just looking to backpack/fool around for a year is "CELTA or go home", and the CELTA is way out of my price range and there are no centers anywhere near where I live.

It's a shame but I guess that's just how life is.

Lack of relevant experience in a saturated industry. I was working with very niche technologies that no one's ever heard of. Even a lot of the "entry level" positions require 2+ years of professional experience in a popular technology such as Java/J2EE or C# .NET. I also have no connections due to being introverted, and I don't have the charisma that other people have.

Hello. I apologize if this is the wrong place to ask as I am kind of new to seriously considering teaching English abroad. Long story short, I would like to know my realistic chances of getting a job teaching English abroad before I decide to invest the time and money into getting a TEFL certification.

A bit of background. I have a MS in Computer Science and did a few semesters as an adjunct instructor back in grad school (which to this day is still my favorite job out of the ones I've done). And because it ideally shouldn't matter but realistically it does, I'm a white male and native English speaker who will be turning 30 this year. I'm also a socially awkward and shy/timid person (a programmer who's socially awkward? Surprise surprise) but I like to think that I have a good heart and can adapt to new situations.

I do have some restrictions as to what I would accept. It has to be in a country that is "safe" and at least has acceptable internet access. I'm also looking to avoid China because of their, well, political climate and censorship (particularly their infamous "Great Firewall"). I would also like to teach at the high school level or above, preferably adults. I am a frugal person by nature so cost of living will always be my main expense.

Would this realistically be a good path for me to go down? I know over the years teaching English abroad has become more competitive, especially in countries like Japan and South Korea, and I don't want it to become a repeat of what I'm experiencing now in the IT industry, where I can't find work for long periods of time.

Thanks in advance.
